guard: a spawn failure returns the lifecycle facts the manager already had (blockedOp, headState, opId, remedy) instead of a connector timeout or opaque string
completionMarker: A. a failed goal terminal carries the lifecycle-blocked facts the manager already had
why: THE LIVE OCCUPANT. A manager-side lifecycle refusal (frozen issuance gate, retiring
alias) was knowable at the throw site and died at the ControlReply string boundary.
The spawn caller then waited out SPEC 13.6 and printed a timeout, or the connector
scrubbed the rest to 'unknown'. The operator spent the next attempts on the wrong
layer. This fixture grades the PROPAGATION, not the underlying lifecycle defect.
THREE DROP SITES, THREE MUTATIONS. Follow collapsing a failed terminal to a bare
message is the wait-timeout twin. MeshAgent.managerInvoke stripping the suffix is
the peer-facing twin. cotal_spawn ignoring ControlReply.details is the tool twin.
Any one of them returning is this issue half-alive.

mutations.name: follow drops the lifecycle details off a failed terminal, so the spawn caller sees a bare message
mutations.find:
const merged = details ?? (fromAccept ? [fromAccept] : undefined);
    return { ...attributed, reply: { ...attributed.reply, ok: false, data: undefined, error: { code: terminal.state, message, ...(merged ? { details: merged } : {}) } } };
mutations.replace: return { ...attributed, reply: { ...attributed.reply, ok: false, data: undefined, error: { code: terminal.state, message: raw } } };
mutations.expectRed: the lifecycle-blocked marker is on the reply the spawn caller sees
mutations.cell: the lifecycle-blocked marker is on the reply the spawn caller sees
mutations.note: The follow path used to take only `data.error`/`data.reason` as a string. Restoring that drop means the marker never reaches the spawn caller even when the manager committed it on the terminal.

mutations.name: managerInvoke stops rendering the lifecycle suffix, so a thrown envelope becomes a bare code:message
mutations.expectRed: and the rendered string names blockedOp, headState, opId, and remedy
mutations.cell: ...and the rendered string names blockedOp, headState, opId, and remedy
mutations.note: Cell C drives a thrown envelope through the real managerInvoke. Without the suffix the structured details may still sit on the ControlReply, but the string an agent reads is the old opaque line.

mutations.name: cotal_spawn ignores ControlReply.details and prints only the raw error string
mutations.find: if (!reply.ok) return err(`Couldn't spawn ${name}: ${renderLifecycleBlocked(reply.error ?? "manager refused", reply)}`);
mutations.expectRed: cotal_spawn reports the lifecycle facts, not an opaque manager refusal
mutations.cell: cotal_spawn reports the lifecycle facts, not an opaque manager refusal
mutations.note: Cell D stubs spawn with a BARE message plus details, which is exactly the ControlReply shape before this fix. If the tool does not render the details, the operator sees the frozen-gate sentence with no opId and no remedy.
